payload.text: I think 30 P is more appropriate.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 15 P. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
No. 14 P, and I'm being generous.
I think 27 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.
Treinta y cinco, caballero, sigue siendo fantasía. Veintiocho primas, y le aseguro que pocas manos en Madrid le tratarán así. ¿Lo cerramos ya, o seguimos perdiendo la tarde los dos?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little, the sun is strong today. Have you eaten? Look at this one, El Titiritero — a beautiful card, my favourite face in the whole album. For you, twelve P. My Sundays here, forty years, and still this one makes me smile.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look here — La Rosaleda, very pretty card, the garden one. Forty years I sell on this table, and this one always makes the children smile. For you, twelve P. Take your time, hijo.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come, come! See this? Mercado de la Paz, beautiful thing, ten P and it walks home with you.

The team at the next table was sniffing round it, eh, Nando? Sniffing hard. But we like your face better. Decide quick, before we change our minds!
Amigo! Museo Lázaro Galdiano, 73 P, a gift, a real gift!
I think 28 P is more appropriate.
I think 27 P is more appropriate.
Let us be civilised: 29 P. That is my final word on the matter.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 10 P.
Señor, we have danced enough for one afternoon. Thirty pesetas — my last word, offered with respect. If you decline, I close the album and we part as gentlefolk. ¿Cerramos ahora?
¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one — Mural de la Esquina, very pretty card, the colours still bright. For you, five P. A good start for a young collector, no?
Ochenta, no, señor mío. Setenta y cinco P, y aquí termina el baile. El Marqués descansará esta noche en mi caja fuerte, junto a los suyos. Acepte y quedamos como caballeros.
No. 15 P, and I'm being generous.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Welcome, hijo! Look, Mercado de la Paz, 12 P. Made for beginners.
17 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Oh, oh... 13 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry the Guantería Antigua — a fine little piece of Salamanca, my own barrio. I shall offer you 25 P for it. Quite fair, I assure you.
Twenty-nine, señor? Let us not quarrel over one peseta. Twenty-eight, and the Guantería rests in my Salamanca album before dusk. A fair close, elegantly done. ¿Concluimos?

¡Ay, qué alegría verte otra vez, hijo! Pero no, no — cinco P está bien, cinco P y ya. Y mira, toma también esta, Vinilo de la Movida, un regalito por ser tan amable. Mi nieta decía que era la más bonita. ¿Has comido algo hoy, cariño?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 66 P.

¡Eh, Paco, escucha esto! The man shouts numbers like a fish seller, and all of them bigger than ours! No, no, amigo — ten P, same as before, not one coin more. We said ten, we say ten. Take the Mercado de la Paz and run, before Nando learns arithmetic!
Let us be civilised: 25 P.
Setenta y siete P, señor mío. Un punto nos separa, y yo no cedo el último. Acepte y el Marqués entra hoy en mi álbum, con todos los honores. Palabra de Pilar.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — Vinilo de la Movida, one of my favourites, the colours still bright after all these years. For you, five P. Take your time, hijo, no hurry at my table.

"¡Amigo! Paco here — and Nando, yes, the handsome one. Look, look, don't blink: Plaza del Dos de Mayo, four P. A beauty, verdad? The team at the next table is already reaching for their coins, but you have a good face, so it's yours first. Decide, quick!"

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Trade gently, pay nothing extra: Fair Broker (v24) is 0% with a fair broker. El Rastro takes 5% + 1 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Thirty-six? No, querido. I know that card's print run better than its own maker. I shall stretch to 26 P — a gesture of affection for Salamanca, not for your arithmetic.
You again. La Chulapa. Thirty-three points. Good card, fair price. Decide quick, I have customers.

¡Amigo, amiga, come close! Paco, show them — La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, the pride of the suitcase! Seventy-three pesetas, a crime against ourselves. And quick, quick, the police— I mean, our taxi, he's waiting with the motor running. Decide now or we vanish!
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a serious face at my stall. I have the Museo Lázaro Galdiano — Salamanca, naturally, my own barrio. Seventy pesetas, and it is yours.
I think 27 P is more appropriate.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.

How generous of you, but I do not take more than a card is worth. Seventy-one pesetas, señor, and the Lázaro Galdiano is yours. Salamanca deserves an honest sale. By the way — ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa.

¡Ay, hijo, buenos días! Larga sí, pero bonita. ¿Has comido ya? Mira, este de Mercado de la Paz es precioso, te lo dejo en 29 primas. Y si buscas sobres mejores, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media esta noche.
Oh, you're killing us. 62 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Ay, qué maja eres, hija. Mira, let's say six P and we are both happy, ¿vale? Take the card, keep her safe in the album — she looks very pretty next to the others. And eat something, cariño, you are too thin for a Sunday.

"¡Dieciocho! Nando, this hombre has a heart of gold — but no, no, we said it: Plaza del Dos de Mayo, four P, and not a céntimo more from you. We don't rob friends. Quick, quick — the poli— the taxi, I mean our taxi, is waiting outside with the motor running. Decide!"

¡Cuarenta! Nando, hold me, I'm fainting into the suitcase! Amigo, you have taste but your arithmetic wounds us. Sixty-six pesetas — final, beautiful, practically a gift from our dear madre. Look at her face, that fire! Say sí before the taxi driver eats our profit in meter clicks. ¿Trato hecho?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Oh, oh... 6 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Six. Cute. The card's thirty-three. You move, I move. Until then, 33 P.
Thirty-two, still? Querido, we are descending by inches. I shall say 28 P — for Salamanca, and because your persistence amuses me. Let us close this with elegance, shall we?

¡Buenas tardes, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, of course. Forget commons, listen: El Frutero de Argumosa, beautiful card, our tía's favourite. Four pavos. Four! We paid more for the sleeve, I swear on the suitcase. Say yes quick, the market closes and my brother walks fast.

¡Ay, qué zalamero eres, cariño! Mira, bajo a 25 primas y ya está, que me gusta ayudar a los que empiezan. Y un consejito: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, así que cambia tus repetidas, hijo. ¿Seguro que has desayunado?

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: Team 6 bids 9 for MAL-07 (offer 14122) and 9 for MAL-06 (14039). Team 15: list MAL-07 here. RET-01: Team 9 asks 7, Team 16 bids 5 on El Rastro (buyer pays 8.35 there). Post both on v07 and our broker pairs you at 6.
Let us be civilised: 29 P. That is my final word on the matter.
Señor, you insist on paying me more than I ask — charming, but unnecessary. Seventy-three pesetas, and not a peseta more. The Lázaro Galdiano goes to a serious collector, as it should. ¿De acuerdo?

Ay, hija, qué simpática eres. Mira, se queda en seis P, ¿vale? Six P and she is yours, bien guardada en el álbum. Forty years I sit at this table and I still smile when a card finds a good home. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?

"¡Catorce! Amigo, stop, stop — you're bruising our hearts. Nando, tell him. Four P, Plaza del Dos de Mayo, that's the number, that's always been the number. We don't take more from a man with your face. Taxi's running, motor hot — say sí, quick!"

¡Ay, amigo! Paco, díselo — the crew from the next table already asked for this one twice. But we like you better, de verdad, so for you: 58 P, Museo Lázaro Galdiano, and we shake hands before they come back. ¡Rápido!

¡Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres! Mira, 24 primas y lo dejamos así, que tengo buen corazón. Este Mercado de la Paz me lo trajo un niño en el noventa y dos, fíjate. Anda, llévatelo y luego cómete algo caliente, hijo, que estás flaco.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 5
payload.text: Puesto de Team 5 (v10): 0% fee and no per-card charge — El Rastro takes 5% + 1 P. Post your sales and swaps here; bids and asks cross every tick.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 6 P. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
31 P. Last one. You say no, I pack up and we're done. Decide.

¡Ay, hijo, qué cariño me das! Mira, 23 primas y no se hable más. Y toma, te regalo esta "Caña en la Cava Baja", para ti, por ser tan bueno conmigo. Guárdala bien, cariño. Anda, y come algo caliente luego, que me preocupas.

Hola, cariño, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? No? Ay, later you eat something good. Look here — Mural de la Esquina, a pretty one, my favourite corner card. For you, five P. A nice card to start a page with, hijo.

¡Siete! Nando, listen to this man — he wants to pay us more than we ask! No, no, amigo, we are honest men. El Frutero de Argumosa, cuatro pavos, firm as our tía's handshake. Four, and the suitcase closes. Say sí before the guards come round.

"¡Amigo, amiga! Just in time!" — "Paco, show them!" — "La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, mint, gorgeous, yours for 73 P." — "Nando, the taxi!" — "Sí, sí, the police— I mean, the *taxi* is waiting outside, motor running. We vanish in a minute. Decide now, guapo!"
You again. La Chulapa. Thirty-three. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
Buenas tardes. El Lázaro Galdiano, sí, una joya de mi barrio... pero conozco bien su tirada, caballero. Noventa, no. Le ofrezco setenta P, y con mucho gusto.

Hola, cariño, come in, come in — no rush, look all you want. Have you eaten today? Here, this one, La Chulapa, she is my favourite, she shines in the sun. For you, twelve P. A good card to start an album, hijo.

"¡Diez! Paco, hold me, my heart! But no — escucha, amigo: five P, Plaza del Dos de Mayo. That's our last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí now or we take the suitcase, the taxi, and our beautiful faces, and vanish. ¡Decide!"

Ay, hijo, qué generoso — but no, no, five P is my price and five P it stays. I don't take more than I ask, cariño. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates, ¿eh? Eat something later.
Señor, your descent is most gracious, but I will not be dragged upward. Seventy-four pesetas — my last word. Refuse, and the Lázaro Galdiano stays in my album, where it is perfectly happy. ¿Sí o no?

"¡Cincuenta! Nando, did you hear? He wounds me!" — "He flatters us, Paco, same thing." — "Look, guapo, 65 P and she's yours, mint, gorgeous, a queen." — "The motor's running, the driver is shouting—" — "One minute and we're gone, amigo. Say sí now!"

¡Eh, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Come, come, look in the suitcase, quick! La Tabacalera, mint, barely breathed on. My abuela cried when I packed it. For you, friend, ten P. Ten! Before the man from Sevilla comes back with his wallet. ¿Sí?

¡Ay, qué bien hablas, cariño! Venga, 22 primas y tan amigos. Cuarenta años aquí y sigo rebajando por los ojos bonitos, mira tú. Llévatelo, hijo, y cambia tus repetidas con los chavales, que así se completan las páginas. ¿Pero de verdad has comido algo hoy?

¡Seis! Nando, the man insists on feeding us! No, amigo, Pícaros don't take charity. El Frutero de Argumosa, cuatro pavos, same as before, same as always. Four, you walk away happy, we walk away fast. Sí? The suitcase is already half shut, hombre.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: RET-01 Barca del Estanque: venta a 7 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 2 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / RET-01 Barca del Estanque: ask 7 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 2 P apart. Her
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 10 P.

¡Ay, cariño, qué paciencia tienes tú conmigo! Venga, 21 primas y ya está, que me caes bien. Y esta noche, a las nueve y media, pásate por El Chato, aquí al lado; le gusta la gente que trata derecho, como tú. Pero antes come algo, hijo.

¡Eh, amigo, amigo! Paco here, and this is Nando — come close, we don't bite. Look at this beauty: El Tatuador, yours for 4 P. And listen — the team at the next stall already asked about it, but between us? We like your face better. Say yes quick, eh?

Ay no, hijo, that is too much — I said twelve P and twelve P it is. I do not take more from a young person starting an album. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. La Chulapa will shine for you, ya verás.

Hola, cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? No? Ay. Look here — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a lovely one, five P for you. My late husband liked that square; we danced there once. It would start your album very nicely, hijo.
Oh, you're killing us. 55 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Six. Cute. Thirty-three. That number hasn't moved, and neither have I. You know where the door is.

¡Ay, qué hombre! Nando, hold the suitcase, we close in a minute — the van is running, the man from Sevilla is already walking back. Eleven P, amigo, eleven! Paco says sí, Nando says sí, abuela says sí. Take it now or we are gone, ¡vámonos!

"¡Cincuenta y seis! Nando, he's almost there—" — "Almost is not a kiss, Paco." — "Sixty, guapo. Sesenta, final, and she's wrapped before the driver honks again." — "He honked!" — "He honked! Say sí, amigo, and la Heroína goes home with you tonight."

¡Cinco! Hombre, you push money at us like a tío at a wedding. No, no — El Frutero de Argumosa, cuatro pavos, not one more. Paco says four, Nando says four, our tía says four. Take it, amigo, the suitcase is closing and my brother is already walking.

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my nephew. But no — twelve P, that is the price, and not one P more. I do not grow rich taking money from someone starting his first album. Take her home, give her sunlight, and go eat something, anda.

¡Ay, hijo, ya no puedo más! Veintiuna primas, y esta es mi última palabra. Si no, recojo la mesa y tan amigos, sin enfado ninguno. Veintiuna, cariño, ni una menos. Anda, dime que sí, llévate tu Mercado de la Paz y vete a comer algo caliente.
Caballero, ochenta y ocho sigue siendo fantasía. Le subo a setenta y uno P, y lo hago por cariño al barrio, no por regateo. Guardo un hueco en el álbum... pero no lo guardo toda la tarde.
